svg.title: An internally flipped generating type II pair has no normal product state or expectation
svg.desc: A normal expectation gives a scalar state on the commuting factor, hence a normal product state. Its GNS multiplication unitary identifies the join with the spatial tensor product. A finite intrinsic corner puts the internal symmetry inside a diffuse finite tensor product, contradicting the exact L2 flip obstruction. The existential source question remains open.

g.text: Normality would force the forbidden spatial flip.
P,Q: type II factors · P and Q commute · P ∨ Q = M · S = S* ∈ M · S² = 1 · SPS = Q
Suppose a normal expectation EP: M → P exists.
For b ∈ Q, aEP(b) = EP(b)a for every a ∈ P; hence EP(b) = χ(b)1.
For a normal state φ on P, ψ = φ ∘ EP gives ψ(ab) = φ(a)χ(b).
No faithfulness assumption on EP, φ or χ · (5D.10)–(5D.11)
Any normal product state ψ on M gives a GNS multiplication unitary.
V([a]φ ⊗ [b]χ) = [ab]ψ; product inner products agree exactly.
Joint generation makes V onto; normal GNS representations of factors are faithful.
Therefore M ≅ P ⊗̄ Q by a ⊗ b ↦ ab · Lemma 5D.1, Theorem 5D.2
Choose p ≠ 0 finite in P, q = SpS, and r = p ⊗ q.
SrS = r; rSr is a unitary in (pPp) ⊗̄ (qQq) implementing its flip.
Both compressed factors are diffuse finite · Proposition 5D.3
Lemma 5C.2: the L² flip intertwiner is zero. Contradiction.
No normal product state; no normal expectation onto either copy.
Theorem 5D.4 · applies to both finite and infinite type II copies
Mutual relative-commutant equality is unnecessary for this obstruction.
A different full source pair would have to be nonexpected.
Connes assumes no expectation. This necessary condition leaves other-pair existence open.
Human-source target: Connes, Corollary 11 and Sakai note, author PDF 44–45.
